title: IG Metall metal workers stage warning strikes in Bavaria

tea.why: Failed collective bargaining negotiations and employers offering a 1.3 percent pay rise.
tea.want: A five percent increase in pay and a combination of employment security, investments, and competitiveness.
tea.changed: Nov 17: IG Metall Bavaria announced a escalation to 24-hour warning strikes, with the Audi plant strike in Ingolstadt scheduled for Friday, Nov 20.

summary: Metal and electrical industry workers represented by the IG Metall union have announced a wave of 24-hour warning strikes across Bavaria as part of an ongoing collective bargaining dispute. Following failed negotiations and an un-upgraded 1.3 percent pay offer from employers, the union leadership escalated actions. Staged warning strikes and rallies are slated for multiple sites, including the Audi plant in Ingolstadt on Friday, November 20, alongside actions at BMW and other facilities. Previous rallies in Ingolstadt earlier in the month saw thousands of participants, with the union reporting 15,000 attendees and police estimating 8,000. The union demands a 5 percent wage increase and addresses matters of job security.
response: No official response reported in the sources.
